chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Ubayd ibn Zur'arah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who enters into marriage with a woman, then she claims the dowry from him, he said: When he has entered with her, the immediate (dowry) has become due.

key_terms.دَخَلَ بِهَا: He entered with her (consummation of marriage)
key_terms.مَهْرُ: Dowry (mahr) given by the husband to the wife
key_terms.هَدَمَ الْعَاجِلَ: Demolished the immediate (legal idiom meaning the immediate debt has become due)

ai.seo_question: When does the husband become obligated to pay the immediate dowry in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In al-Istibsar, Shaykh al-Tusi records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the chain of Ubayd ibn Zurara, clarifying that consummation (dakhala biha) triggers the immediate liability of the dowry (mahr al-'ajil), rendering it a crystallized debt regardless of prior payment status. This ruling underscores the legal principle that the physical union serves as the definitive condition for the wife's right to claim the agreed-upon portion, a cornerstone of Shia fiqh regarding marital financial rights.
